title: Leibniz for a fixed quotient sheaf action and horseshoe boundary
statement: Let X, B, C, p, I and i form a square-zero short exact algebra extension as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Fix compatible injective resolutions IA, IB, IC and chain maps alpha,beta lifting i,p, with short exact rows and a short exact global-sections complex [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let mu:C(X) -> End(I) be a unital ring homomorphism such that for each global f, each open U, each local lift b of f restricted to U, and x in I(U), i((mu(f))_U(x))=b*i(x). Let d:C(X) -> H1(X,I) be the global-sections degree-zero comparison followed by the transported snake boundary of the fixed resolutions, with H1 given by [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Then d(fg)=H1(mu(f))(d(g))+H1(mu(g))(d(f)) for all f,g. This conclusion asserts only the identity for the given action and boundary; it asserts no existence of actions.

proof.text: Use module_exactness_local_lifting for the underlying epimorphism p to choose a common open cover with lifts b_a of f and c_a of g. The products b_a*c_a lift fg. The image of i is the sectionwise kernel, so their overlap differences have unique preimages z_f,z_g,z_fg in I. Triple differences telescope to zero, giving Cech cocycles. The product of two image sections of i vanishes: hw implies each image is killed by p, and the square-zero hypothesis applies.

On every overlap, b_a*c_a-b_b*c_b=(b_a-b_b)*c_a+b_b*(c_a-c_b). Apply the local-lift action equation to g with lift c_a, and to f with lift b_b; commutativity gives i(z_fg)=i(mu(g)(z_f)+mu(f)(z_g)). Injectivity of i on sections identifies these cocycles. This is purely ring algebra once the cocycles and the given lift-action equation are available.

The local-lift boundary theorem identifies the three Cech classes with the connecting classes. Its square-zero hypothesis on image sections follows from hw as above. The canonical Cech comparison is natural in module endomorphisms and additive. Thus it sends the preceding cocycle equality to the Leibniz identity in H1. A uniform reversal of the difference convention reverses all three classes and preserves the identity; use a single convention throughout.

Compute connecting classes in the chosen compatible resolutions. The horseshoe delta-functor theorem and comparison maps between resolutions give equality of transported snake boundaries for the identity ladder on the short exact sequence. Equivalently, choose a compatible resolution to compute the Cech-to-derived comparison and compute its connecting map with the same snake construction. Naturality of the resolution isomorphisms identifies this with the supplied IA,IB,IC,alpha,beta; the augmentation in degree zero is toRightDerivedZero. Hence the map d in the statement gives the same connecting classes, and the identity applies to d.

theorem square_zero_horseshoe_boundary_leibniz (X : Scheme.{u})
    (B C : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (p : B ⟶ C)
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ commAlgebraSheafModule X.sheaf B)
    (hw : i ≫ (commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor X.sheaf).map p = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk i ((commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor X.sheaf).map p) hw).ShortExact)
    (hsq : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (x y : B.right.obj.obj (op U)),
      p.right.hom.app (op U) x = 0 → p.right.hom.app (op U) y = 0 → x * y = 0)
    (IA : InjectiveResolution I)
    (IB : InjectiveResolution (commAlgebraSheafModule X.sheaf B))
    (IC : InjectiveResolution (commAlgebraSheafModule X.sheaf C))
    (α : IA.cocomplex ⟶ IB.cocomplex) (β : IB.cocomplex ⟶ IC.cocomplex)
    (hαβ : α ≫ β = 0)
    (hιA : IA.ι ≫ α = (CochainComplex.single₀ _).map i ≫ IB.ι)
    (hιB : IB.ι ≫ β =
      (CochainComplex.single₀ _).map ((commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor X.sheaf).map p) ≫ IC.ι)
    (hH : ∀ k : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval _ (ComplexShape.up ℕ) k)).ShortExact)
    (hΓ : ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map
      ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ))).ShortExact)
    (μ : C.right.obj.obj (op ⊤) →+* End I)
    (hlift : ∀ (f : C.right.obj.obj (op ⊤)) (U : X.Opens)
      (b : B.right.obj.obj (op U)) (x : I.val.obj (op U)),
      p.right.hom.app (op U) b = C.right.obj.map (homOfLE le_top).op f →
      @id (B.right.obj.obj (op U)) (i.val.app (op U) ((μ f).val.app (op U) x)) =
        b * @id (B.right.obj.obj (op U)) (i.val.app (op U) x)) :
    let d :=
      (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).toRightDerivedZero.app
          (commAlgebraSheafModule X.sheaf C) ≫
        (IC.isoRightDerivedObj (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace) 0).hom ≫
        hΓ.δ 0 1 rfl ≫
        (IA.isoRightDerivedObj (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace) 1).inv
    ∀ f g : C.right.obj.obj (op ⊤), d.hom (f * g) =
      ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace 1).map (μ f)).hom (d.hom g) +
        ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace 1).map (μ g)).hom (d.hom f)
